name: Thermage / monopolar RF
lead: Thermage is a brand of non-ablative monopolar radiofrequency (RF) treatment used in clinics for skin tightening of the face, neck and eyelids. It heats the dermis with RF energy while the surface is cooled, with the aim of tightening lax skin and softening fine lines without surgery.[1][2] The device was first sold as ThermaCool and is now marketed as Thermage FLX.[3]

RF skin tightening in general is described as heating the dermis to stimulate collagen, elastin and hyaluronic acid production and tissue remodelling, with a dermal target temperature of about 67 degrees C cited.[1] Early studies from 2003 to 2004 reported improvement in periorbital and cheek or neck laxity after single treatments.[2][4]
Published studies are mostly small and company-linked device studies, and sources note adverse effects including pain and, rarely, fat loss or scarring.

paras: RF energy heats the dermis, and the heating is said to stimulate collagen production and remodelling. Penetration depth depends on electrode configuration, with monopolar, bipolar and unipolar designs described.[1]

A multicentre study of 86 subjects receiving one ThermaCool treatment around the eyes reported that independent scoring of blinded photographs showed improved Fitzpatrick wrinkle scores in a large majority of treated areas at six months.[2] A study of 50 patients with mild to moderate cheek or neck laxity evaluated one treatment for safety and efficacy, and a randomised comparison of one versus two treatments was run in 20 patients with middle and lower face laxity.[4][5] A 2006 retrospective review of over 600 treatments was undertaken to measure actual rates of side effects.[6]

Sources report that some patients had pain requiring sedation, that improper technique may cause skin dents, and that fat necrosis and atrophic scarring have been reported, though newer techniques reportedly address this.[1]

Published studies include multicentre and single-centre device studies in the periorbital area, cheek and neck, and lower face.[2][4][5][6] Registered trials include Thermage FLX on face, neck and eyelids (n=25), a controlled safety and effectiveness study (n=164), a feasibility comparison of Ulthera versus Thermage for face and neck (n=20), and a monopolar RF facial wrinkle study (n=284).[7][8][9][10]

timeline.event: Monopolar RF skin tightening in clinical use; the 2006 review dates use to May 2002.[6]

card.summary: Clinic radiofrequency heating for mild-to-moderate skin laxity; small studies report modest improvement.
card.note: Evidence is mostly small device studies; pain and, rarely, fat loss or scarring are reported.

quick.overview:
Thermage is a clinic treatment that uses monopolar radiofrequency to heat the dermis while cooling the surface, aiming to tighten loose skin on the face, neck and eyelids.

Early studies reported improvements in wrinkle and laxity scores after a single session. Evidence is mostly small device studies.
quick.mechanism: RF energy heats deep skin, said to stimulate collagen and elastin and remodel tissue.
quick.risks: Pain that sometimes required sedation, skin dents, and rare fat necrosis or scarring have been reported. It is delivered by trained clinicians.
